text:
Brazil reaffirms national jurisdictions' primary duty; the ICC acts when a State is unable or unwilling. Nonparties have no Rome Statute obligations, while resolution1970 under ChapterVII requires full Libyan cooperation. Other States and organizations are urged to cooperate. The Court lacks its own enforcement instruments; cooperation requests must conform to the Statute and relevant Council resolutions.

We welcome improving Prosecutor-Libyan cooperation and support victims, witnesses and communities inside and outside Libya, including engagement with their representatives. All serious-crime victims deserve equal treatment without politicization or selectivity. No ICC judgments have been delivered in the Libyan situation; evidence and investigative progress are welcome. We seek more information on the four inquiry lines and hope fruitful cooperation advances complementarity-based justice.
